512.prompt: I felt embarrassed after forgetting my lines at rehearsal. Everyone was kind, but I still wanted
512.completion:
to disappear. That feeling bothered me so much I made myself look at it. I realized the experience gave me the same feeling I had in third grade when the class laughed at my science project. In both cases, I thought at the time that I was different and deficient.

Now I see that what these experiences gave me was a choice. I could relive these moments through the lens of scarcity — believing there was something wrong with me or something not so great about who I was to be embarrassed. Or I could see these moments as reminders that I get to choose what to be.

I chose to be joyous.

Choosing to feel joy, for me, means letting go of trying to be someone different and appreciating who I am. I feel joyous when I am not putting up a barrier in front of my feelings. All I have to do is be with my feelings as they come and allow whatever is there to be there. As a result, I am here, present and not trying to be someone else and I no longer see my experience of feeling joy as a source of embarrassment. I see joy as my strength.

If you are someone who finds it hard to do this, let me introduce you to a friend of mine who is the perfect person to help.

Meet Liana.

Liana remembers the first time she felt joy as a child. She remembers being five years old; it was nighttime and her family was looking for owls. She was with her grandmother, sister and dog. Eventually, they found an owl, and as Liana looked up, the owl flew overhead. She was overfilled with joy for several moments until they stopped seeing the owl. When they went inside, Liana’s mom was so tired she told Liana she needed to go to bed. Liana felt disappointed and went to her room. It wasn’t until the next day when the memory came flooding back to her, and she experienced the joy all over again that the story was fully completed.

For Liana, like for me, experiencing joy every day is a spiritual practice, and as hard as the practice can be at times, it is always worth it. As you can see from Liana’s photo, she is someone who can teach us a thing or two about finding joy and sharing the experience.

To benefit from this lesson, it’s important to remember that every moment is an opportunity to find joy, and you can begin today.
